author: economics_audit agent
scope: Initial 10 mechanism catalog, not 10000 completed systems and not a parameter/configuration search. Known mechanisms are mapped honestly to existing repository overlap.
decisionRule: Count a system only if economic mechanism, state/action/payoff structure or contractual cash-flow source changes substantially. Shared parent mechanisms are disclosed. Thresholds, lookbacks, symbols, algorithms fitting the same target and filter/exit combinations do not multiply the count.
clarificationPending: Whether new means established systems new to this engine or original mathematical inventions.

as.title: Avellaneda and Stoikov, High-frequency trading in a limit order book
as.verifiedClaim: Inventory-aware optimal quoting under stylized stochastic price and market-order arrivals; does not establish current crypto profitability.

arb.title: Makarov and Schoar, Trading and Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets
arb.verifiedClaim: Historical cryptocurrency exchange price segmentation and limitations on arbitrage capital; not a current executable opportunity.

carry.title: BIS Working Paper 1087, Crypto carry
carry.verifiedClaim: Dated crypto basis and scarce arbitrage capital/leveraged demand; margin and liquidation risks limit the strategy.

kraken_contract.title: Kraken linear multi-collateral derivatives specifications
kraken_contract.verifiedClaim: Funding is a signed transfer between long and short positions, accruing continuously and settling at hour end or net-position change.

kraken_fee.title: Kraken fee schedule
kraken_fee.verifiedClaim: Published entry-tier spot maker/taker rates are 0.40%/0.80%; account qualification is separate.

flow.title: Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov, The Price Impact of Order Book Events
flow.verifiedClaim: Order-flow imbalance was associated with short-horizon price changes in US equities; contemporaneous association is not a crypto prediction guarantee.

trend.title: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen, Time Series Momentum
trend.verifiedClaim: Historical own-return predictability across 58 traditional futures/forwards; not current BTC/ETH profit evidence.

vrp.title: Cboe S&P 500 Market-Neutral Volatility Risk Premia Optimized Index methodology
vrp.verifiedClaim: Option premium strategy with purchased protection; an equity-index methodology, not measured cryptocurrency returns.

option_payoff.title: Deribit position builder primer on basic option strategies
option_payoff.verifiedClaim: Option combinations can have equivalent terminal payoffs; contract conventions and hedged premia matter.

deribit_instrument.title: Deribit public/get_instrument
deribit_instrument.verifiedClaim: Provides settlement/quote currencies, expiry, strike, fees, contract type and quantity increment; example payload is not a current live contract.

deribit_fee.title: Deribit fees
deribit_fee.verifiedClaim: Trading, delivery and liquidation costs have distinct rules and require product-specific normalization.

uniswap.title: Uniswap v3 Core whitepaper
uniswap.verifiedClaim: Concentrated-liquidity positions own a bounded segment of an automated reserve curve.

uniswap_fees.title: Uniswap protocol fees
uniswap_fees.verifiedClaim: LP fee receipts and protocol allocation depend on pool/version; live pool state must be read.

lvr.title: Milionis et al., Automated Market Making and Loss-Versus-Rebalancing
lvr.verifiedClaim: An AMM liquidity provider bears stale-price adverse selection measured against a rebalancing benchmark.

liquidation.title: Aave health factor and liquidations
liquidation.verifiedClaim: Eligible liquidators repay borrower debt and receive collateral plus a bonus; competition and current governance parameters matter.

systems.name: Two-sided inventory-constrained limit-order liquidity provision
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Earn an executable bid/ask spread by supplying immediacy; retain only the portion exceeding fees, inventory risk and adverse selection.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: Impatient counterparties pay for immediacy; informed counterparties can transfer losses to the market maker.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman stochastic control with inventory utility and marked point-process fills; queue-aware state extends the stylized Avellaneda-Stoikov model.
systems.illustrativeEquation: Canonical reservation price r_t=S_t-q_t*gamma*sigma^2*(T-t); realized episode net=q*(sale_bid_or_ask-purchase_bid_or_ask)-fees-inventory_unwind_cost.
systems.repoOverlap: Existing directional maker/taker routing and a queue-aware entry shadow are reusable, but are not a full two-sided inventory controller.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: Potentially new complete controller; published 40 bp spot maker fees imply about 80.32 bp gross buy-to-sell appreciation even if both fills are maker, before inventory losses. Actual eligible fees must be verified.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Record full opportunities without trading; reject if achievable completed spreads cannot exceed exact fees and adverse markouts on intended capital.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Funded multi-market price-parity routing
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Buy an economically identical transferable asset where executable asks are lower and sell owned inventory where executable bids are higher; route cycles are grouped here.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: Market segmentation, restricted capital movement and asynchronous price discovery maintain price differences until arbitrage capacity closes them.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Capacity-constrained min-cost circulation with negative-log conversion costs and explicit venue inventories; multi-stage stochastic control for non-atomic legs.
systems.illustrativeEquation: One matched quantity: net=q*(bid_B*(1-fee_B)-ask_A*(1+fee_A))-rebalance_cost-failed_leg_cost; a friction-adjusted cycle requires product(executable_conversion_rates)>1.
systems.repoOverlap: No complete multi-venue funded parity router was found in inspected execution/carry/strategy sources. Existing book walking and decimal inventory primitives are reusable.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: Public quote screening is feasible after a second source adapter. Trades require funded inventory at both venues; a visible spread alone does not prove simultaneous execution or cheap capital recycling.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Normalize identical claims and record synchronized executable capacities; reject when fees plus inventory-recycling and failed-leg costs erase discrepancies.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Dated spot-futures cash-and-carry
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Capture initial positive futures basis as the dated contract settles against its defined index, while owning offsetting spot.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: Demand for leveraged upside and scarce balance-sheet capacity can make a dated claim expensive relative to funded spot.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Cash-flow matching, term-structure valuation and robust collateral optimization with settlement-index basis state.
systems.illustrativeEquation: For matched linear exposure: net=q*(F_entry-S_entry+S_exit-I_settlement)-all_execution_costs; excess_return also subtracts the declared capital hurdle.
systems.repoOverlap: Already implemented as research economics and monitoring; saved study found no dated contract inside its 30-to-90-day policy window.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: Existing local infrastructure; presently no qualifying opportunity established. The simple basis formula requires same quantity and correctly normalized linear payoff; futures margin can require cash long before expiry.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Reuse the monitor with newly captured quotes and verified fees; require positive net under explicit settlement/index and collateral stress.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Spot-perpetual funding-transfer carry
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Collect positive perpetual funding while holding offsetting spot; funding may reverse and there is no maturity that locks total profit.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: Long perpetual holders pay shorts when the venue funding rate is positive; the transfer compensates carrying opposing derivatives exposure.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Partially observed funding-state model with optimal stopping and joint basis/collateral state; continuous signed cash-flow integration.
systems.illustrativeEquation: Long spot/short perp net=integral(q_t*absoluteFundingRate_t dt)+q*(basis_entry-basis_exit)-fees-repair_costs for constant matched q.
decisionActions: stop when stressed remaining income no longer covers liabilities
systems.repoOverlap: Existing carry monitor, continuous accrual and horizon selector; prior fee frontier and zero-cycle screens did not qualify.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: Not new to the engine research set. Lower spot fees alone failed all saved paths; missing future funding cannot be treated as zero or fixed.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: On prospective synchronized rates/books, compare complete paired P&L with zero/last-rate funding baselines and all declared costs.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Persistent directional-trend risk allocation
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Exploit conditional positive serial dependence if gradual information incorporation or sustained demand makes past direction predict future net return.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: No contractual payer. The hypothesized source is predictable demand/information adjustment; raw market appreciation alone is not strategy alpha.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Sequential drift inference/change-point detection with optimal switching between funded long and cash; volatility-aware allocation.
systems.illustrativeEquation: Value requires E[w_t*(S_future/S_t-1)-transaction_costs | information_t]>benchmark; changing a lookback does not create a new mechanism.
decisionActions: switch only with causal signal and cost hurdle
requiredPublicData: complete finalized spot bars or events
systems.repoOverlap: Already present as weekly SMA/hysteresis, CUSUM trend and momentum rotation research.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: Easy to reproduce locally; existing weekly parent has positive history but sparse episodes, and daily variants failed. Not a newly discovered economic source.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Freeze the existing rule and measure genuinely later fully costed returns versus cash and an exposure-matched benchmark; retain all prior failures.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Order-flow information forecasting
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Predict future executable price changes from persistent informed or liquidity-demanding order flow before those changes are incorporated.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: No contractual payment. A predictive information advantage must survive competition and the cost of acquiring immediacy.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Marked point-process/Hawkes or state-space filtering of order-flow imbalance and book depletion, with a causal forecast horizon.
systems.illustrativeEquation: Empirical contemporaneous relation DeltaPrice≈beta*OFI motivates a hypothesis only; trading requires E[future_exit_bid-current_entry_ask-fees | past_events]>0.
systems.repoOverlap: Existing distribution features and deterministic signal code already use order-flow imbalance, microprice and related pressure.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: Not structurally new. A contemporaneous US-equity regression cannot establish prospective crypto profit; spot entry-tier taker costs create a high hurdle.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Estimate strictly future executable markouts on every event decision; compare with a no-information baseline after measured latency and costs.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Option insurance-risk premium allocation
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Receive option premium for bearing convex volatility/jump losses when prices exceed the expected full cost of payouts and hedging.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: Option buyers pay for convex protection or upside exposure; the seller accepts tail losses rather than collecting free yield.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Constrained option portfolio optimization under stochastic volatility/jumps and expected shortfall, with protected downside and discrete hedging.
systems.illustrativeEquation: Delta-hedged short-option local approximation: dPnl≈0.5*Gamma_long*S^2*(sigma_implied^2-sigma_realized^2)*dt-costs; jumps, discrete hedging and model error invalidate treating this as guaranteed equality.
decisionActions: select fully funded or risk-bounded option exposure
systems.repoOverlap: No complete option data, payoff-normalization, hedging or accounting system found in inspected sources; current linear cash-flow primitives are insufficient.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: New system and new data stack. An equity-index VRP methodology does not establish a positive crypto premium. No borrowing or option orders are part of this catalog.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Acquire complete causal surfaces and build an independent funded payoff ledger; reject if protected-tail strategy net does not beat matched risk/capital benchmarks.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Static derivative payoff-dominance dislocation search
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Buy a cheaper contract portfolio and sell an equivalent or dominated one when executable prices violate exact terminal payoff relations after costs.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: Inconsistent pricing of claims to the same contractual cash flows; unlike volatility selling, profit does not require forecasting realized volatility if all contract and execution conditions hold.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Linear or mixed-integer programming over normalized piecewise-linear payoff vectors, lot sizes, bid/ask costs and collateral feasibility.
systems.illustrativeEquation: Find quantities z with initial_cash_cost(z)+cost_reserve<0 and terminal_payoff_z(s)>=0 for every admissible settlement state s; enforce funding and no-uncovered-liability constraints.
decisionActions: request no trade when legs cannot be locked
systems.repoOverlap: No payoff-vector or static-dominance optimizer found. Inverse and linear instruments must not share an unnormalized payoff formula.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: High-quality new read-only falsifiable screen, not a demonstrated profit strategy. A grid of settlement states is insufficient unless payoff breakpoints and tails prove the inequality globally.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Normalize instruments, prove dominance at exact breakpoints/tails and record synchronous executable capacity; reject all opportunities invalidated by costs or unavailable combo execution.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Automated-market-maker liquidity capital control
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Earn actual swap-fee receipts by supplying a reserve curve, after stale-price adverse selection and capital/rebalancing costs.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: Swappers pay protocol-defined fees; arbitrageurs can extract value when the pool price lags external markets.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Constant-function market maker geometry and stochastic impulse control of concentrated-liquidity ranges; loss-versus-rebalancing benchmark.
systems.illustrativeEquation: Pool LP advantage versus matched rebalancing=earned_LP_fees-LVR-gas-range_reposition_costs-other_costs; pool token price gain alone is not fee alpha.
systems.repoOverlap: No AMM adapter or on-chain inventory/fee-growth ledger found. CLOB maker execution does not implement reserve-curve ownership.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: A genuinely different state/action/payoff mechanism from CLOB quoting, but shares the same broad economic parent (liquidity service); do not claim it is an independent risk premium.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Use archived pool state to reconcile actual LP fees and compare funded positions with matched external rebalancing after gas; do not annualize a displayed fee APY as total return.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

systems.name: Funded liquidation-service inventory acquisition
systems.sourceOfExpectedReturn: Receive collateral at a protocol-defined liquidation bonus for paying an eligible borrower debt, then liquidate acquired collateral after all execution costs.
systems.economicPayerOrConstraint: The protocol pays the bonus from borrower collateral to incentivize rapid debt repayment and preserve solvency.
systems.mathematicalControlModel: Event-triggered constrained optimization of debt/collateral exchange with transaction-order competition, gas bidding and robust post-fill liquidation value.
systems.illustrativeEquation: net=executable_collateral_sale_proceeds-debt_repaid-gas-builder_costs-fees-failed_attempt_costs; protocol bonus percentage is not net return.
systems.repoOverlap: No protocol liquidation bot or on-chain execution/receipt system found. Existing trading risk liquidation checks are unrelated to earning protocol liquidation bonuses.
systems.costAndExecutionFeasibility: Distinct economic service, but competitive and infrastructure-heavy. This catalog permits observation/simulation only and assumes funded capital; no flash borrowing, wallet transaction or lending action is performed.
systems.firstFalsificationTest: Replay actual historical eligible positions with conservative inclusion order and funded capital; reject paper opportunities other liquidators already consume before achievable inclusion.
systems.mathematicalOriginality: Established mathematical/economic mechanism; no claim of a new theorem or invention.

sequenceMeaning: Order of falsifiable evidence collection, not a ranking by demonstrated profit. EC01 requires a fee-feasibility check first.
excludedFromCounts: Separate triangular versus cross-venue routes under identical price-parity economics
Model-family changes without a new economic mechanism
Existing trend/carry/order-flow variants described as inventions
Fees, sizing and risk controls counted as standalone return sources
limitations: No new backtests or executable profit measurements were run for this catalog.
Public research establishes models or historical mechanisms, not current account-specific profitability.
No current cross-venue/option/on-chain opportunities were fetched or claimed.
Novelty assessment covers inspected repository sources and is not a proof no related code exists elsewhere.
Liquidity provision entries EC01 and EC09 share an economic parent; architecture differences are disclosed rather than counted as independent premia.
